adds.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
adds.text: On the bus to Prague, Betty tells Peter his new glasses look good on him. Back at Newark, she and Ned tell him they have broken up.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: A classmate whose new glasses Betty compliments.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A classmate who likes Peter's new glasses and tells him she and Ned split.
adds.evidence: Betty Brant page, Traveling to Prague and Return to New York City: she remarks on Peter's new E.D.I.T.H. glasses on the bus; at Newark she and Ned compliment Peter on his relationship and tell him they ended theirs.

adds.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
adds.text: Flash taunts Peter on the plane to Europe for being too poor to fly. On the bus to Prague he grabs Peter's new glasses and puts them on, and Peter accidentally knocks him out getting them back.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Classmate Flash taunts on the trip, who knocks him out over a pair of glasses.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Classmate who taunts Peter on the trip and grabs his new glasses.
adds.evidence: Flash Thompson page, Trip to Europe and Traveling to Prague: airplane taunt ('flies over the poor neighborhoods'); grabs the E.D.I.T.H. glasses and Peter accidentally knocks him out.

adds.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
adds.text: When Harrington announces a four-hour opera in place of the Carnival of Lights in Prague, Flash protests that none of them ever wanted to go to the opera.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Trip chaperone who swaps the carnival for the opera.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A student who scoffs at the opera plan.
adds.evidence: Flash Thompson page, Opera House: exchange 'Do you have any idea how much opera tickets cost?' / 'No. Because none of us have ever wanted to go to the opera. Ever.'

adds.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
adds.text: When Peter heads to Berlin, MJ and Ned cover for him with the class. In London the two break away together to lead Mysterio's drones from their classmates.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: A friend who covers for Peter with MJ, then flees the drones beside her.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A friend who covers for Peter with Ned and fights the drones beside him.
adds.evidence: Michelle Jones page, Trip to Czech Republic and Battle of London: she and Ned tell the class Peter is staying with family; knowing Mysterio is after them, they run to lead him away from the class and hide in the Tower of London.

adds.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
adds.text: On the flight to Europe, Harrington reshuffles the students' seats and moves MJ into his own spot, next to Brad.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Trip chaperone who reshuffles the plane seats.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A student he moves into his own seat on the plane.
adds.evidence: Roger Harrington page, Plane Ride with Students: 'MJ, stand up. Ned, take MJ's spot. Alright, MJ, you take my spot.' MJ page: she ends up seated next to Brad Davis.

adds.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
adds.text: In Prague Ned covers for Peter by calling his black suit Night Monkey, a European knock-off. When Peter leaves for Berlin, Ned agrees to tell the class he is staying with family.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: A best friend Ned covers for as Night Monkey.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A best friend who covers for Peter's Night Monkey suit and his trip to Berlin.
adds.evidence: Ned Leeds page, Attack on the Prague Carnival: Ned invents the alias Night Monkey to cover for Peter; later he is asked to tell the chaperones Peter is visiting family in Berlin.

adds.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
adds.text: When Harrington announces a four-hour opera in Prague, Ned is the only student who backs the plan, and Harrington thanks him.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Trip chaperone whose opera plan only Ned defends.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A student who alone backs the opera plan.
adds.evidence: Roger Harrington page, Trip to the Opera: 'When Ned Leeds voiced his approval over this, Harrington thanked him.'

adds.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
adds.text: Harrington seats Peter beside himself on the flight to Europe and tells him how his wife faked being blipped. On the bus he orders Peter to sit down, unaware Peter is stopping a drone strike.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: A chaperone who seats Peter beside him and shares his wife's story.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A student he sits beside on the plane and scolds on the bus.
adds.evidence: Roger Harrington page, Plane Ride with Students and Eventful Bus Ride: sits next to Peter and tells him about his wife's deception; 'Peter, plant your fanny in that seat and buckle up' while Peter stops a combat drone.

adds.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
adds.text: When the class scatters in London, Flash follows Ned, MJ and Betty, and they hide together from Mysterio's drones in the Tower of London.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: A classmate who follows Ned's group and hides from the drones with them.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A classmate Flash follows in London, hiding with him from the drones.
adds.evidence: Flash Thompson page, Battle of London: 'upon seeing Jones, Leeds, and Brant run separate from the group, Thompson followed them'; they hide in the Tower of London vault with Happy.

none.why: May's scenes are the Blip fundraiser, Peter's packing, a call with Happy present, and the Newark pickup; none shows her dealing with MJ. A fan-wiki line that MJ and Ned tell Peter's aunt he is staying in Berlin is not backed by May's page or the plot.

none.why: May and Ned share no scene or exchange here; May only deals with Peter and Happy.

owner_calls.question: Maria Hill is listed in Spider-Man: Far From Home, but on screen she is Soren in disguise the whole time and the real Hill never appears. Keep Far From Home in Hill's appearances?
options: Keep as is (the face is Hill's, credited as Hill)
Drop Far From Home from the real Hill's appearances
owner_calls.evidence: Post-credits scene reveals Fury and Hill as Talos and Soren in disguise.
